metadata.case_name: CHU MAN TING v. KWAN KAM KEI & ANOTHER

injuries.description: Depressed skull fracture which caused swelling of the brain.
source: The severity of the collision caused Man Ting to lose consciousness. On arrival at hospital, the Glasgow Coma Scale was 7/15, her blood pressure was elevated 136/178 and her pulse was 150/min. She sustained a depressed skull fracture which caused swelling of the brain.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of vault of skull, unspecified

injuries.description: Diffuse cerebral oedema with traumatic subarachnoid haemorrhage.
source: The CT scan of the brain showed diffuse cerebral oedema with traumatic subarachnoid haemorrhage.

injuries.description: Left sided haemothorax (a collection of blood in the chest cavity).
source: There was left sided haemothorax (a collection of blood in the chest cavity).
X-ray examination showed a fractured left clavicle,

injuries.description: A comminuted fracture of the right forearm (distal radius and ulna).
source: X-ray examination showed ... a comminuted fracture of the right forearm (distal radius and ulna)
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of lower end of both ulna and radius

injuries.description: Fracture of the 1st, 2nd and 3rd metacarpals of the right hand.
source: X-ray examination showed ... a fracture of the 1st, 2nd and 3rd metacarpals of the right hand.

injuries.description: A crack fracture of C3 and C4 of the vertebral body.
source: A scan of the cervical spine revealed a crack fracture of C3 and C4 of the vertebral body.

manifestations.description: Headaches associated with dizziness, occurring daily and lasting from one to two hours brought on by mental tasks.
Dizziness occurring daily and lasting for up to three or four hours; dizziness caused loss of balance on two occasions leading to further falls and fractures.
Poor short term (recent) memory; difficulty retaining study material.
Change in personality including irritability, lack of inhibition and socially inappropriate behaviour (for example singing during class).
Poor sense of direction; needs to be accompanied by an adult when visiting unfamiliar places.
Obesity resulting from excessive over-eating (weight rose to 93.6 kg); described as 'comfort eating'.

Diminished intellectual functioning; present IQ measured at 119 and an expert's conservative estimate of pre-accident IQ at 138; overall diminution in intellectual capacities affecting school performance.
An increased risk of post-traumatic epilepsy compared to the normal population (experts provided differing statistical presentations).
Reduced social functioning; poor personal relations at school, victim of bullying and loss of good friends.

treatments_received: Managed in Intensive Care Unit for about two weeks

losses.description: Diminution in overall intellectual capacities, reduction in IQ and academic performance; diminished intellectual 'amenity' for which the plaintiff was compensated.

losses.category: Loss of ability to pursue education
losses.description: Forced to repeat Form 1 and Form 2, two years behind her chronological age, reduced prospects of obtaining a university place (including medical school).
Poor personal relations at school, victim of bullying, loss of good friends and reduced social functioning.

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: Poor sense of direction and need to be accompanied when visiting unfamiliar places.
Change in personality including irritability, lack of inhibition and socially inappropriate behaviour (for example singing during class).
